EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  October 24, 2016

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ called the meeting to order, the time being 7:00 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Velveth Schmitz
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano
Susan Brtis
Bill Kemp
Patricia Harik
Carol Dean-Porter
Victor Yoo
Pam Schachter

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT – EXCUSED
Lisa Hawkins

STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 26, 2016
MEMBER KEMP requested that MEMBERS DEAN-PORTER, YOO, and HAWKINS be
indicated as having “Excused Absences” for the September 26, 2016 meeting due to technical
issues that the City was experiencing emailing the Committee’s agenda packets. CHAIRMAN
SCHMITZ reminded COMMITTEE MEMBERS that they should be watching for the
Equestrian Committee agenda packet, or a meeting cancelation notice, emailed on the
Thursday before the fourth Monday of each month. She also noted that all of the City’s
Committees will be re-organized in January.

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER KEMP

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE SEPTEMBER 26, 2016 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS AMENDED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
OCTOBER 24, 2016  1
 AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
MEMBER SHINN apologized for not attending the September 19, 2016 Park and Activities
Commission meeting where proposed equestrian fee changes were discussed.

POTENTIAL HORSE ARENA SITES ON PALOS VERDES LANDFILL
The Community Services Director provided a verbal report thanking MEMBERS DEAN-
PORTER, SHINN, and SILVANO for touring two potential sites on October 19, 2016 with the
Community Services Director, City’s Maintenance Supervisor, and the Palos Verdes Landfill’s
on-site Engineer. He reported that they had first looked at the native land along the south
side of the site, located between the Peter Weber Equestrian Center’s (PWEC) rear boundary
and Hawthorne Boulevard. The Subcommittee determined that this area was either too close
to homes, too narrow, or not large enough to support the construction of a dressage-sized
horse arena. The Subcommittee next went to the former LA County Recycle Center adjacent
to Crenshaw Boulevard and found this site to be large enough and not likely to cause issues
for nearby residents. The Community Services Director reviewed aerial and ground photos of
the site which may be able to support a 70 foot wide by 180 foot long arena. MEMBER
SCHACHTER noted that the size of the proposed new arena would be smaller than the
Chandler Park horse arena, which is 100 feet wide by 200 feet long.

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ stated that there would be several hurdles to overcome before
approvals could be obtained from Los Angeles County and the Sanitation Districts of Los
Angeles County. She noted that an election for the Fourth District Supervisor’s Office would
be taking place in two weeks and that the new Supervisor would have to be brought up to
speed on the City’s equestrian needs before considering whether to approve the proposed
arena project. The Community Services Director stated that additional hurdles the proposed
construction project could face may include an environmental impact report (EIR), which could
be costly, and usually takes several months to complete. In addition, he noted that the former
Recycle Center site would require demolition of the structures and asphalt, which could
almost double the estimated $100,000 cost to construct this sized horse arena. MEMBER
DEAN-PORTER responded that the arena may be able to be built on top of the asphalt, as
has been done in other equestrian centers. Finally, the Community Services Director noted
that access to the proposed arena site may be lengthy if users are required to use the Palos
Verdes Landfill’s southbound access road from the Landfill Loop trail on the top deck of the
landfill. The on-site Engineer had indicated that the landfill road which went south from the
entry of the former Recycle Center off of Crenshaw Boulevard (toward PWEC) had regular
truck traffic on a daily basis, which would make it potentially hazardous for use by equestrians
to gain access to the proposed arena site.

MEMBER SHINN suggested that the large turn-out arena at the Peter Weber Equestrian
Center be made into a public arena to relieve the overcrowding at the Chandler Park riding
arena. Further, she believes that this arena could be leased to licensed horse trainers which
use the Chandler Park arena. COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER indicated that when she had
boarded a horse at PWEC she had noticed that the facility’s arenas were mostly empty in the
mornings. She noted that the PWEC Concessionaire is agreeable to allow the City’s licensed
trainers to use these arenas in the mornings for a $1,000 per month fee.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
OCTOBER 24, 2016, 2016  2
 MEMBER DEAN-PORTER reminded the Committee that the PWEC arenas were previously
open to the public for riding and training, but due to an incident involving Grace McGettigan in
the 1990’s, the PWEC arenas were closed to the public and became only available for PWEC
trainers and boarders. CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ inquired whether the Committee should pursue
making one or more of the PWEC riding arenas available to the public or continue
investigating the proposed construction of a new arena on the former Recycle Center site.
MEMBER DEAN-PORTER responded that she believes the Committee should pursue both
arena options.

The Community Services Director suggested that instead of moving too quickly pursuing
either public arena option that the PWEC Operator could be invited to the next Equestrian
Committee meeting to discuss the possibility of PWEC allowing public riding and training. In
regards to the upcoming election, he stated that staff would contact the new Supervisor’s staff
as soon as they would be able to meet to update them on the City’s need for an additional
public riding arena and discuss the former Recycle Center as a potential site.

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER DEAN-PORTER

  TO DIRECT STAFF TO INVITE THE PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER
  CONCESSIONAIRE TO THE NOVEMBER 28, 2016 EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE TO
  DISCUSS ALLOWING PUBLIC USE OF THE FACILITY’S ARENAS AND TO INFORM
  THE NEW FOURTH DISTRICT SUPERVISOR’S STAFF ABOUT THE CITY’S NEED
  FOR A PUBLIC RIDING ARENA ON THE PALOS VERDES LANDFILL SITE.

Hearing no objections, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ so ordered.

HOWLETT PARK EQUESTRIAN STRUCTURES UPDATE
The Community Services Director provided an overview of the steps taken to develop the
specifications to replace the Horse Show Office, Horse Show Judges Booth, and Dressage
Show Judges Booth in the Ernie Howlett Park Equestrian Center. He thanked COMMITTEE
MEMBERS SCHACHTER, DEAN-PORTER, and SHINN and Los Serranos Award Circuit
Chair, Becky Martin for all their assistance on this project. A recent meeting between staff
and Alan Pre-Fab Buildings owner was helpful in finalizing the bid specifications, developing
cost estimates, and creating a timeline for completing this project.

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ inquired whether COMMITTEE MEMBERS has any other additions or
corrections to the specifications in the staff report. In response, MEMBER SHINN suggested
that the City purchase a water truck due to the watering issues in Howlett Park arenas #1 and
#2.

MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN

  TO  APPROVE  THE  HOWLETT  PARK  EQUESTRIAN  STRUCTURE
  SPECIFICATIONS AS PRESENTED.

Hearing no objections, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ so ordered.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
OCTOBER 24, 2016  3
 EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE
EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG.

COMMITTEE REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
None.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ACTION ITEM OF OCTOBER 17,
  2016
The Community Services Director reported that all of the City’s licensed horse trainers had
been mailed letters inviting them to attend a meeting with City staff on November 14, 2016 at
7:00 p.m. to further discuss the horse trainers’ usage of the City’s public arenas in regards to
proposed permit fee changes. In response to MEMBER SHINN’S request to participate at
this meeting, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ indicated that she had made a decision after meeting
with the City Manager to only have the Assistant City Manager and Community Services
Director meet with the licensed horse trainers at this meeting and present the meeting’s
outcomes at the November 28, 2016 Equestrian Committee meeting.

B.  WATER TRUCK PURCHASE
The Community Services Director will obtain quotes for new and used water trucks and
determine whether it would be more feasible to purchase or rent a water truck prior to the
upcoming horse show season.

C.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH EQUESTRIAN/PEDESTRIAN CROSSING
The Community Services Director will provide an update on the new equestrian/pedestrian
crossing project on Palos Verdes Drive North, east of Eastvale Road on November 28, 2016.

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 8:04 p.m.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
OCTOBER 24, 2016  4
 Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
